caution_findings.evidence_context: Strongest direct membrane-damage evidence is for C16-KKKK-NH2; other lipopeptides have activity and biophysical membrane-interaction context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C16-KKKK-NH2 has direct membrane-damage evidence in live/dead microscopy assays for S. epidermidis and E. coli at MIC multiples.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct cellular membrane-damage evidence is shown for C16-KKKK-NH2 under the tested conditions; it should not be generalized to every lipopeptide as an identical quantified mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ITC/FTIR measurements support peptide interaction with negatively charged lipid membranes and LPS, with counterion-dependent behavior for C16-KKKK-NH2.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: reported lipopeptides and negatively charged model membranes/LPS
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biophysical membrane interaction is source-supported, but exact organism-level killing mechanism remains bounded to the direct assays above.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CG MD simulations support rapid adsorption of C16-KKKK-NH2 to POPG/POPE and RaLPS-containing membrane models and suggest calcium-ion release from RaLPS/Lipid A regions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational support is not treated as a standalone direct antimicrobial mechanism assay.

mechanism_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication; direct claims are limited to membrane damage/interactions supported by local XML, supplement figures, ITC/FTIR tables, and CG MD outputs.
